title: Squeeze a soft-grip clothes peg off a basket rim and clip a hanging photo's free corner to a photo wire
instruction: The photo hangs from the wire by one peg. Peg its other top corner to the wire too.
context: Hanging photos, drawings and cards on a wire or string with clothes pegs is an everyday way to display them at home, in classrooms and shops, and the same peg squeeze-and-clip is how washing is pegged out. A peg opens only while its handles are squeezed, so it must be squeezed off the basket, kept squeezed in transit, and let go with its V-shaped jaws straddling a 1.2 mm wire and a 0.3 mm print together, without knocking off the photo already hanging by one peg.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Wire: a 1.2 mm steel photo-display wire, taut between two brown posts at x 17 and 49, along x at y 0, 8.5 cm above the table. Photo: a 127 x 89 mm print (beach scene, 0.3 mm, 2.8 g) hanging upright beside the wire on its +y side, centred at x 30 [B: 31], top edge 1.2 cm above the wire, held by one peg at its far top corner (0.5 cm in from its end). Pegs: soft-grip wooden clothes pegs, 72 mm long, legs 5 x 10 mm, pivot 30 mm from the jaw tips, torsion spring 0.25 N m/rad (closed jaws press at about 3.6 N), handles splayed 8 degrees with green rubber grip pads, 6 g. Basket: a fixed blue plastic basket (12 cm deep, rim 9 cm tall) with its near wall along x at y -15 [B: -16.5]; two spare pegs clipped on that wall's rim at x 36 and 40 [B: 35.5 and 39.5], legs across the wall. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the photo is knocked off the wire (its top edge 1 cm or more below where it hung). Otherwise 1.0 once a second peg holds the photo's near top corner on the wire, let go and still, for 2 s: its jaws closed on the wire, within 2 cm of the photo's near end, the photo's top edge between its legs, both grippers over 4 cm away, the photo still. 0.5 if a peg is closed on the wire, let go and still (anywhere). 0.25 if a peg has been taken off the basket (moved 2 cm). Else 0.
reset_notes: Unclip the new peg and put it back on the basket's rim; leave the photo hanging by its first peg at its far top corner, top edge 1.2 cm above the wire.
fidelity: Pegs, photo and wire are rigid. Each peg is an articulation: two wooden legs on a pivot with a torsion spring, a groove for the wire and rubber grip pads on the handles; wood and paper do not deform. The wire is modelled as a taut rigid 1.2 mm rod between fixed posts (a real wire sags a little). The print is a rigid 0.3 mm card.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right gripper hovered by the basket; no peg taken); demo: 1.0 (second peg on the near corner at step 285)
